pass_a_gloss: The first having been proved in this manner, as gold is proved in a smelting pot, the second was being led to the mockery; whose skin with the hairs the attendants of tyrannical rawness having dragged off, they were calling the one who had suffered to repentance, asking further whether he will eat of the things sacrificed to idols before the body is punished for him member by member. And as he denied the repentance, he was led to the next torture, guarding his stand until the last breathing. For being in no way shattered nor yielding toward the toils he said these things to the impious one: you rather, avenging demon, loose us out of the present living, but the king of the cosmos will raise us up, having died on behalf of his laws, into an eternal coming-back-to-life of life.
pass_b_english: When the first had been tested in this way, as gold is tested in a furnace (Wisdom of Solomon 3:6), the second was led off “to be mocked” (2 Maccabees 7:7). The servants of the tyrant's cruelty “tore off his skin with the hair” and called on the sufferer to change his mind, asking whether he would eat food offered to idols “before his body was punished limb by limb”. When he refused to change his mind, he was led to “the next” torture, keeping his resolve to his last breath. For he was not broken in the least and did not give way to the pains, but said this to the ungodly man: “You rather, you accursed wretch, are releasing us from this present life; but the King of the world will raise us up, who die for his laws, to an everlasting renewal of life” (2 Maccabees 7:9).

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. 24); the old English was a digest: it dropped the testing 'as gold in a furnace', the call to change his mind and the question about food offered to idols, and added a closing line ('Avenging spirit, learn that tortures loose the body but bind the tortured unto judgment') that is not in the Greek.

choices.issue: σὺ μᾶλλον, ἀλάστορ (2 Macc 7:9 σὺ μέν)
choices.choice: Koetschau prints μᾶλλον; translated 'You rather', as printed.
'change his mind' (to abandon his stand), not the Christian sense 'repentance'.
"the ungodly king" changed to "the ungodly man": the Greek has τὸν ἀσεβῆ, no word for king.

lemmas.gloss: return to life, renewal of life
